caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 91 of 1997.
lawyer:
KZ Alam, Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record. 
Md Mujibur Rahman, Senior Advocate instructed by Mvi Md Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record — For Respondent. No. 1
 Not represented—Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Zakir Hossain Khan (Md) and others ------ Petitioners
VS.
SM Jillur Rahman and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: This petition for leave to appeal by the accused-petitioners is from the judgment and order dated 10-6-97 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Revision No. 726 of 1996 preferred by the informant-respondent, setting aside the order dated 1-9-96 passed by the 3rd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Sessions Case No. 120 of 1993 and cancelling the bail granted to the accused-petitioners, directing them to surrender before the 3rd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka forthwith. 

 2. Since the bail matter of the accused-petitioners has travelled upto this Division previously and since the judgment of the High Court Division contains in details the background of the case, it is not necessary to recount the facts of the case fully. 

 3. Suffice it to say that the accused-petitioners previously filed Criminal Revision No.1940 of 1992 for bail in the High Court Division which by judgment and order dated 8-9-93 found that there are strong prima facie materials to connect the accused-petitioners with the throwing away of deceased Bilal from the 6th floor of the Head Office building of Titas Gas which resulted in his death. The High Court Division directed the accused-petitioners to surrender before the trial Court on or before 22-9-93. The accused-petitioners preferred Criminal Petition for Leave to appeal No. 96 of 1993 which was dismissed on 26-10-93 by this Division with the observations that there were sufficient materials before the High Court Division in believing that the accused-petitioners were guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The case is ready for trial. The impugned order does not call for any interference. 

 4. Further, in criminal Revision No. 2003 of 1993 under section 561A CrPC the accused-petitioners filed an application for bail which was rejected by the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 7-8-94 on the ground that the accused-petitioners do not fall within any of the categories of accused persons mentioned in the proviso to section 497CrPC and that there is a strong prima facie case under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code against them and that a charge has been framed against them. Against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division the accused-petitioners moved Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 29 of 1994 which was also dismissed by this Division. The accused petitioners thereafter filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 216 of 1995 before the High Court Division under section 526 CrPC and they obtained an ad-interim order of bail. But the Rule was discharged with the direction of surrender before the trial Court forthwith. The accused-petitioners again moved the High Court Division in criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2908 of 1995 and prayed for bail and they were given ad-interim bail in that Rule. While making the Rule absolute the High Court Division observed that in all fairness it ought not to have issued the present Rule and granted ad-interim bail. However, since during pendency of this Rule the petitioners enjoyed the privilege of bail the Rule was made absolute on condition that the 2nd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka where the trial was pending will conclude the trial within 3 months from the date of receipt of the copy of the order and the order of bail will continue to remain effective for 4 months. This judgment is dated 16-4-96. The State moved the Appellate Division in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 103 of 1996 against the said order passed by the High Court Division but in dismissing the said petition the Appellate Division observed that one prosecution witness has been examined at the trial and the next date of examination of prosecution witnesses has been fixed on 29-6-96. This is a case where an interference of this Division is called for but in view of the fact that the trial is the interest of justice will be served if the accused-petitioners continue to be on bail till 15-7-96. 

 5. One accused Moniruzzaman moved the High Court Division in Criminal Revision No. 540 of 1995 against the rejection of his prayer for discharging him from the case under section 526 CrPC and the Rule was made absolute. The State again came to the Appellate Division in Criminal Appeal No. 20 of 1996 against the said order of the High Court Division. The appeal was dismissed with the order that the bail already granted earlier to the added accused-petitioners will continue till 31-8-96. 

 6. The accused-petitioners again moved the High Court Division for bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 216 of 1995 invoking the jurisdiction under sub-section (4) of section 339C CrPC which was rejected with the observation that 360 days was not over and the accused-petitioners are not entitled to any relief by way of bail. 

 7. After 31-8-96 the accused-petitioners surrendered before the 3rd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka on 1-9-96 and then prayed for continuation of their bail earlier granted. The learned Additional Sessions Judge by order dated 1-9-96 found that the higher Courts of the country have not placed any embargo in the granting of bail and as he has the authority to grant bail in such a case and as the Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the State was making preparation for withdrawal of the case the accused-petitioners may be enlarged on bail and accordingly they were enlarged on bail. 

 9. The High Court Division found that the two grounds for enlarging the accused-petitioners on bail are that the State is considering the withdrawal of the case as submitted by the Additional Public Prosecutor and that the trial Court has the power to grant bail. The High Court Division observed as follows: 

 11. Mr. KZ Alam, learned Counsel for the accused-petitioners, has harped on the old theme that the accused-petitioners did not misuse the privilege of bail, but he could not overcome the High Court Division''s strong indignation at the assumption of power by the trial Court to grant bail when in unmistakably clear terms the superior Courts time and again found that there are strong prima facie materials in support of the accused-petitioners involvement on a charge under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code and that they do not fall under the purview of the proviso to section 497 CrPC. The bail granted by this Division to be effective upto 31-8-96 was not extendable by the trial Court. After all these observations all that was needed to be done was to conclude the trial as per direction of the High Court Division. The assumption of power by the trial Court to grant bail afresh to the accused-petitioners was a highly imprudent action for which the trial Court richly deserved the judicial indignation expressed by the High Court Division. The plea that the State was taking steps to withdraw the case is being held out as a carrott for a long time and the trial Court should not have been swayed by that fact. In a later judgment of this Division in the same case in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 350 of 1997 it has been observed that the Public Prosecutor and all his deputies were found to be partisan and they are siding with the defence and that it would be fair and reasonable in the interest of justice for the Government to appoint a Special Public Prosecutor for this particular case and not leave the matter in the hands of the incumbent Public Prosecutor or his deputies.
